Default adduct and fragment rules

Source: R/data.R
adductRules.Rd

adductRules is a list with two data.frames, positive and negative, with the adduct and in-source fragment rules from the 'commonMZ' package (commonMZ::MZ_CAMERA()), in CAMERA's rule format and expanded to one to four molecules per ion. The list is long on purpose: annotations are meant as hints, so a missed true relationship is worse than a coincidental one. The ranking of annotateAdducts() puts the best supported hypothesis first.

Usage

data(adductRules)

defaultAdductRules(polarity = c("positive", "negative"))

Format

A list of two data.frames with the columns:

name

rule name, e.g. "[M+H]+".

nmol

number of molecules in the ion.

charge

charge of the ion.

massdiff

mass added to nmol neutral molecules to form the ion.

oidscore

CAMERA's rule identifier score.

quasi

1 for quasi-molecular ions, which can anchor a hypothesis.

ips

rule score; higher means more common.

Source

Generated from 'commonMZ' (MIT licence, by the same author) with inst/scripts/make-adductRules.R.

Arguments

polarity

character(1), "positive" or "negative".

Value

defaultAdductRules(): a data.frame.

Details

defaultAdductRules() returns the table for one polarity.

Examples

head(defaultAdductRules("positive"))
#>        name nmol charge massdiff oidscore quasi  ips
#> 1    [M+H]+    1      1 1.007276        1     1 1.00
#> 2   [2M+H]+    2      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 3   [3M+H]+    3      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 4   [4M+H]+    4      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 5  [M+2H]2+    1      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75
#> 6 [2M+2H]2+    2      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75
